title: Dysregulation of atrazine-associated core gene networks and risk prediction in human cancers: Insights from integrated transcriptomics and network toxicology analyses.
authors: Chen, Xi; Zhang, Xiangxin; Tang, Ping; Shang, Yifeng; Wang, Yaoyu; Yin, Changqing; Wang, Lianlei; Zhang, Qunye; Liu, Xinyu; Yang, Qing; Yang, Liu
one_liner_zh: 该研究利用转录组和网络毒理学分析阿特拉津相关核心基因网络及癌症风险预测，虽含分子对接和转录因子分析，但核心是基因表达与PPI网络，缺乏蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: Atrazine, a widely used chlorotriazine herbicide, persists in aquatic environments and poses potential carcinogenic risks. While epidemiological studies link atrazine exposure to malignancies, its intrinsic molecular mechanisms across organ systems remain incompletely understood. This study employed integrated network toxicology and transcriptomic analyses to clarify atrazine-associated oncogenic pathways in liver hepatocellular carcinoma (LIHC), kidney renal clear cell carcinoma (KIRC), lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), and sarcoma (SARC). Transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) for these cancers were analyzed to identify atrazine-related genes. Protein-protein interaction networks were constructed and analyzed to identify hub genes. Functional enrichment, immune microenvironment analyses, and survival analysis were performed. Molecular docking validated atrazine-target binding, and independent datasets were used for hub gene expression and pan-cancer relevance validation. We identified 92 (LUAD), 136 (LIHC), 137 (KIRC), and 161 (SARC) atrazine-associated targets. Hub genes including CDC6, MCM5/7, UBE2C, FEN1, CDCA8, and VIM were differentially expressed across these cancers. Enrichment analyses revealed atrazine disruption of core pathways, including cell cycle progression and chromosomal instability, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, metabolic reprogramming, and senescence-associated secretory pathways. Molecular docking confirmed high-affinity binding between atrazine and key targets. Pan-cancer validation implicated these hub genes in multiple additional malignancies. Transcription factor analysis nominated HSD17B8 as a key regulatory node. This study demonstrates that atrazine promotes carcinogenesis by dysregulating conserved networks governing genomic stability, cell proliferation, metabolic adaptation, and immune microenvironment remodeling, providing a mechanistic framework linking aquatic atrazine exposure to multi-organ carcinogenesis and nominating HSD17B8-associated pathways for therapeutic intervention. These findings underscore the imperative for enhanced environmental monitoring of atrazine contamination.
abstract_zh: 阿特拉津（Atrazine）是一种广泛使用的氯三嗪类除草剂，在水生环境中持久存在，并具有潜在的致癌风险。尽管流行病学研究将阿特拉津暴露与恶性肿瘤联系起来，但其跨器官系统的内在分子机制仍未完全阐明。本研究采用整合网络毒理学和转录组学分析，以阐明阿特拉津在肝肝细胞癌（LIHC）、肾肾透明细胞癌（KIRC）、肺腺癌（LUAD）和肉瘤（SARC）中相关的致癌通路。分析了来自癌症基因组图谱（TCGA）的这些癌症的转录组数据，以识别阿特拉津相关基因。构建并分析了蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络以识别枢纽基因。进行了功能富集、免疫微环境分析和生存分析。分子对接验证了阿特拉津与靶标的结合，并使用独立数据集进行枢纽基因表达和泛癌相关性验证。我们识别出92个（LUAD）、136个（LIHC）、137个（KIRC）和161个（SARC）阿特拉津相关靶标。包括CDC6、MCM5/7、UBE2C、FEN1、CDCA8和VIM在内的枢纽基因在这些癌症中差异表达。富集分析揭示了阿特拉津对核心通路的干扰，包括细胞周期进程和染色体不稳定性、上皮-间质转化、代谢重编程以及衰老相关分泌通路。分子对接确认了阿特拉津与关键靶标之间的高亲和力结合。泛癌验证表明这些枢纽基因涉及多种其他恶性肿瘤。转录因子分析提名HSD17B8为关键调控节点。本研究证明，阿特拉津通过失调控制基因组稳定性、细胞增殖、代谢适应和免疫微环境重塑的保守网络来促进致癌作用，提供了一个将水生阿特拉津暴露与多器官致癌联系起来的机制框架，并提名HSD17B8相关通路用于治疗干预。这些发现强调了加强阿特拉津污染环境监测的紧迫性。
